loai: a 3D scene explaining a building or a place
ly_do: R1: X shows a clear, lit, labelled scene whose subject you grasp in seconds. Y is a crude, murky render in which the objects are not identifiable and the caption has low contrast.
R2: X shows a readable, labelled, well-lit scene that explains its subject at a glance, while Y is an ambiguous set of placeholder-looking props that doesn't illustrate a toll.
R3: X shows a clear, labelled cutaway that explains the building at a glance, while Y is an unreadable pile of untextured boxes where nothing visibly says 'toll'.

loai: a map showing where the story happens
ly_do: R1: Y tells you where and what in a couple of seconds with readable text, while X is an unlabeled abstract diagram that conveys nothing without narration.
R2: Y shows a recognisable real place with clear labels and context, while X is an abstract, textless graphic with no clear subject.
R3: Y tells the viewer where and what happened with readable text, while X has no text and no way to tell what the map shows.

loai: a historical/official record: a person, a document or a timeline
ly_do: R1: X shows a real archival photo with a clear caption, while Y is a mostly empty dark slide with one timeline event and a muddy background.
R2: X shows a tangible, instantly understood archival subject with decent composition, while Y is a mostly empty flat slide with tiny text and no visual anchor.
R3: X shows a real person with a clear caption and a tactile composition, while Y is a mostly empty template card with a lone timeline point and tiny text.
